title: Build Wide, Ship Narrow
excerpt: Splitting a finished branch into small PRs used to be the expensive part, so we decided the boundaries before the code existed. That cost collapsed. Now the code can tell you where to cut it.
content_html:
Good engineers plan before they build. The workflow I grew up seeing: write an RFC describing the feature, split it into smaller issues, then build them, each issue often blocking the next. The structure of the work was locked in before a single line of code existed.

This is reasonable. It keeps code reviews manageable and avoids big-bang merges. It also asks you to make your most critical structural decisions at the moment you know the least about the problem.

Before you've built anything, you're guessing: which pieces are separable, how complex each one will be, whether step 3 will force you to rethink step 1. Sometimes you're right. Often you're not, and step 1 gets thrown away. You learned something building it, but you'd have learned it faster by building the whole thing first.

We paid that cost for a good reason: the alternative was building everything and untangling it by hand, and untangling a week of work is harder than planning ahead. Deciding boundaries up front was never about making the build easier. It was about making review possible, and it was the only affordable way to get there. That's the part that changed.

What changed

Three things got dramatically cheaper. Building: an AI assistant turns a clear problem into working code in hours, sometimes minutes. Design: you can interrogate a plan and reshape it at conversation speed. And the one that matters most here, decomposing a finished branch: splitting a week of tangled work into a sequence of small PRs used to be the most tedious part of the job, which is exactly why we avoided it. It's now a prompt.

Two things didn't get cheaper. The first is the judgment half of code review. Agents made the mechanical half (consistency, nits, obvious bugs) nearly free, but they don't settle subtle correctness or the questions around it: does this change belong where it is, will this endpoint shape hurt six months from now. A bot approving your PR isn't the same as you understanding the code, and if you didn't type the code, reading it is how you come to own it. Narrow PRs make that reading possible.

The second is product validation. Running the thing and deciding it's the right thing to build is still slow. What's new is having the whole feature working early enough to show someone before anyone reads a line of it.

So stop pre-deciding boundaries to dodge a cost that no longer exists.

My workflow now looks like this:

  1. Grill the plan until it has real decisions in it
  2. Commit the spec before any code, when the design is novel
  3. Build wide, committing save points as you go
  4. Demo and iterate before anyone reads the code
  5. Split into PRs along the boundaries the code revealed
  6. Merge, cleanup last: pure deletion in its own final PR

Design still goes first

To be clear: this isn't "skip planning and start coding." Before I touch the editor, I have a plan, and every feature starts with an interrogation. I run grill-me, a skill that interviews you about your idea in adversarial rounds until it has real decisions in it. What's the fallback if the API call fails? I run it on everything, including small changes, and it keeps surfacing gaps I didn't know were there.

When the design is novel, the plan becomes a spec committed before any code. On a different project, the first PR was a document: what the feature was, how it would work, where the trust boundaries sat. It merged days before any implementation existed, so the team could push back first.

What never gets committed is a decomposition into PRs. Decide what to build before you build it; decide how to slice it after.

Build wide

Once the design is settled, I build. I often work in steps, but I don't stop at each one to open a PR and wait for review. Everything stays on one branch until it works end to end, across whatever files are in the way.

Commits happen, but they aren't milestones for anyone else. They're save points: a concept is proven, or I'm about to try something risky and want a rope to pull back to. A refactor I finished recently ran to a dozen-plus commits in a single day across dozens of files, with operational messages. Waypoints so I can see where I've been, not a story for a reviewer.

This is the part that makes some engineers uncomfortable, and I understand why: git history is supposed to be the record. But this history never becomes the record. The PRs at the end are cut fresh off main, and the build branch is scratch paper you throw away. Two audiences separated in time, me and the reviewers, and keeping them apart lets you optimize for both.

Demo before anyone reads the code

Once the work is in a good place, I stop and show it. Not as a PR or a code review, but a short video in Slack, or a preview deployment if the change needs clicking. Feedback on working software from the people who will use it, before a single code review starts.

Review is expensive now that the cheap half is automated. Finding out at review time that you built the wrong thing (confusing UI pattern, an endpoint shape that doesn't fit how the frontend uses the data) burns a reviewer's time and your own. A demo catches it while changes are cheap. If it surfaces something that needs rethinking, I run grill-me on the feedback first, so the iteration isn't just vibes.

Ship narrow

The build order is only a rough draft of the split: the steps get regrouped and re-cut. The deletion PR is the clearest example, a unit that only exists at the end, once the new path is in place.

I run one prompt:

Split the current work into the smallest set of independently reviewable PRs, each safe to merge on its own, and each delivering value to the user whenever the work allows. Create a git worktree and branch off main for each. Stack only where a dependency is real; otherwise branch from main. Any removal of the code being replaced goes in its own final PR. Show me the proposed split before creating anything.

How long it takes depends on how tangled the work is, from a few minutes to a few rounds of back-and-forth. Either way, no manual cherry-picking.

That refactor came out as five PRs: two backend endpoints as siblings off main, two frontend views each sitting on top of the backend PR whose data it needs, and a final PR that was pure deletion of the old path. The deletion removed several hundred more lines than the whole feature added. That's the shape of a refactor done in this order.

Two rules I've arrived at by doing this repeatedly:

Stack only when the dependency is real. A frontend view PR depends on its backend endpoint PR, and the branch reflects that. Everything else comes from main. Stacking for convenience creates a rebase chain you'll regret the moment the bottom PR gets feedback.

Cleanup ships last. The old code dies in its own PR, after the new path is live. Mixing deletion with creation confuses reviewers, makes rollback ambiguous, and buries the cleanup in the noise of the feature.

The split is also when I read my own work. Going through the diff PR by PR, at a size I can hold in my head, is the difference between having shipped AI-written code and understanding it. I'd rather find my own problems there.

One practical note: managing a stack burns context fast, so hand the split work to subagents that report back to a main agent. In Cursor, the split-to-prs skill packages this.

What it bought, what it costs

The heavy PRs stay heavy, and they should. The backend ones carried the real architectural risk (new data models, new API surface, trust boundaries), which is where reviewers should spend their attention. The frontend PRs that consume them read in minutes. Small, focused PRs flow. Large ones sit.

The agent review loop is faster at this scale too. At Adapt, we use Adapt itself as a reviewer, an agent with business context from previous work. It comments within minutes of a PR opening, and the exchange (questions, clarifications, a small fix) resolves in under ten. That only works when a PR is small enough to read quickly; a 2,000-line PR mixing several concerns doesn't get that treatment from a human at all.

Merging incrementally also makes deployments easier to manage. If something breaks, you revert one focused change, and your error tracking points at that change instead of an entire merged stack.

Those are the gains. Two costs come with them.

Rebasing. When a reviewer asks for a change on a PR that another sits on, every branch above it needs rebasing. It doesn't happen often, since reviewers usually touch leaf PRs, but when it does you feel it. Keep the chat session that produced the split open: it still holds the split, so you can re-prompt it to update the branches above instead of doing it by hand.

Splitting is not shipping. As I write this, all five PRs from that refactor are still open. A good split makes each PR easy to review and worth merging on its own. An agent does the first for me; the second is my call when I decide what goes in each PR, and my team's when they decide what to merge. Mine sat because I only did the first. Even if all five merge on the same day I keep the review benefit and a clean revert target per change; what I lose is incremental delivery, since nothing reached a user earlier and the deploys land as one batch.

When to reach for it

Good fit: multi-surface features crossing backend and frontend, refactors where you don't know the final shape until you've done it, any work where you'd otherwise be guessing at issue boundaries.

Harder fit: migrations and schema changes that must be sequenced in production, where the ordering is real and you should plan it first. Work that has one obvious place to cut. Features where step 1 cannot ship alone, ever; if everything lands at once, late decomposition buys you incremental review and nothing more.

The heuristic: if you're writing an RFC and guessing at how to break it into issues before you've built anything, that time is probably better spent building. You'll have better answers at the end. I've been testing this across a few projects and it has held up.

The structural decision doesn't go away. It just gets much cheaper when you make it with the code already in front of you.

sentences.zh: 我对所有事情都运行它，包括小的变化，它不断地出现我不知道的差距。

blocks.html_en: When the design is novel, the plan becomes a spec committed before any code. On a different project, the first PR was a document: what the feature was, how it would work, where the trust boundaries sat. It merged days before any implementation existed, so the team could push back first.

sentences.en: When the design is novel, the plan becomes a spec committed before any code.
sentences.zh: 当设计新颖时，计划就成为在任何代码之前提交的规范。

sentences.en: On a different project, the first PR was a document: what the feature was, how it would work, where the trust boundaries sat.
sentences.zh: 在另一个项目中，第一个 PR 是一个文档：功能是什么、它将如何工作、信任边界在哪里。

sentences.en: It merged days before any implementation existed, so the team could push back first.
sentences.zh: 它在任何实施出现之前几天就合并了，因此团队可以先推迟。

blocks.html_en: What never gets committed is a decomposition into PRs. Decide what to build before you build it; decide how to slice it after.

sentences.en: What never gets committed is a decomposition into PRs.
sentences.zh: 永远不会被提交的是分解为 PR。

sentences.en: Decide what to build before you build it; decide how to slice it after.
sentences.zh: 在构建之前决定构建什么；之后决定如何切片。

blocks.html_en: Build wide

sentences.en: Build wide
sentences.zh: 构建广泛

blocks.html_en: Once the design is settled, I build. I often work in steps, but I don't stop at each one to open a PR and wait for review. Everything stays on one branch until it works end to end, across whatever files are in the way.

sentences.en: Once the design is settled, I build.
sentences.zh: 一旦设计确定，我就开始建造。

sentences.en: I often work in steps, but I don't stop at each one to open a PR and wait for review.
sentences.zh: 我经常按步骤工作，但我不会在每一步都停下来打开 PR 并等待审核。

sentences.en: Everything stays on one branch until it works end to end, across whatever files are in the way.
sentences.zh: 所有内容都保留在一个分支上，直到它端到端地工作，无论任何文件都在其中。

blocks.html_en: Commits happen, but they aren't milestones for anyone else. They're save points: a concept is proven, or I'm about to try something risky and want a rope to pull back to. A refactor I finished recently ran to a dozen-plus commits in a single day across dozens of files, with operational messages. Waypoints so I can see where I've been, not a story for a reviewer.

sentences.en: Commits happen, but they aren't milestones for anyone else.
sentences.zh: 承诺发生了，但对于其他人来说它们并不是里程碑。

sentences.en: They're save points: a concept is proven, or I'm about to try something risky and want a rope to pull back to.
sentences.zh: 它们是保存点：一个概念已被证明，或者我正要尝试一些冒险的事情并想要一根绳子拉回来。

sentences.en: A refactor I finished recently ran to a dozen-plus commits in a single day across dozens of files, with operational messages.
sentences.zh: 我最近完成的一次重构在一天之内对数十个文件进行了十几次提交，并带有操作消息。

sentences.en: Waypoints so I can see where I've been, not a story for a reviewer.
sentences.zh: 航点让我可以看到我去过的地方，而不是评论者的故事。

blocks.html_en: This is the part that makes some engineers uncomfortable, and I understand why: git history is supposed to be the record. But this history never becomes the record. The PRs at the end are cut fresh off main, and the build branch is scratch paper you throw away. Two audiences separated in time, me and the reviewers, and keeping them apart lets you optimize for both.

sentences.en: This is the part that makes some engineers uncomfortable, and I understand why: git history is supposed to be the record.
sentences.zh: 这是让一些工程师感到不舒服的部分，我明白为什么：git 历史应该是记录。

sentences.en: But this history never becomes the record.
sentences.zh: 但这段历史永远不会成为记录。

sentences.en: The PRs at the end are cut fresh off main, and the build branch is scratch paper you throw away.
sentences.zh: 最后的 PR 是从主干上新鲜切下来的，构建分支是你扔掉的草稿纸。

sentences.en: Two audiences separated in time, me and the reviewers, and keeping them apart lets you optimize for both.
sentences.zh: 两个受众在时间上分开，我和审阅者，将他们分开可以让您针对两者进行优化。

blocks.html_en: Demo before anyone reads the code

sentences.en: Demo before anyone reads the code
sentences.zh: 在任何人阅读代码之前进行演示

blocks.html_en: Once the work is in a good place, I stop and show it. Not as a PR or a code review, but a short video in Slack, or a preview deployment if the change needs clicking. Feedback on working software from the people who will use it, before a single code review starts.

sentences.en: Once the work is in a good place, I stop and show it.
sentences.zh: 一旦作品到位，我就会停下来展示它。

sentences.en: Not as a PR or a code review, but a short video in Slack, or a preview deployment if the change needs clicking.
sentences.zh: 不是 PR 或代码审查，而是 Slack 中的短视频，或者预览部署（如果需要单击更改）。

sentences.en: Feedback on working software from the people who will use it, before a single code review starts.
sentences.zh: 在单个代码审查开始之前，使用该软件的人员对可用软件的反馈。

blocks.html_en: Review is expensive now that the cheap half is automated. Finding out at review time that you built the wrong thing (confusing UI pattern, an endpoint shape that doesn't fit how the frontend uses the data) burns a reviewer's time and your own. A demo catches it while changes are cheap. If it surfaces something that needs rethinking, I run grill-me on the feedback first, so the iteration isn't just vibes.

sentences.en: Review is expensive now that the cheap half is automated.
sentences.zh: 现在审查很昂贵，因为便宜的一半是自动化的。

sentences.en: Finding out at review time that you built the wrong thing (confusing UI pattern, an endpoint shape that doesn't fit how the frontend uses the data) burns a reviewer's time and your own.
sentences.zh: 在审核时发现您构建了错误的东西（令人困惑的 UI 模式、不适合前端使用数据方式的端点形状）会浪费审核者和您自己的时间。

sentences.en: A demo catches it while changes are cheap.
sentences.zh: 演示可以捕捉到它，而更改的成本却很低。

sentences.en: If it surfaces something that needs rethinking, I run grill-me on the feedback first, so the iteration isn't just vibes.
sentences.zh: 如果出现需要重新思考的问题，我会首先对反馈进行“烧烤”，因此迭代不仅仅是共鸣。

blocks.html_en: Ship narrow

sentences.en: Ship narrow
sentences.zh: 船窄

blocks.html_en: The build order is only a rough draft of the split: the steps get regrouped and re-cut. The deletion PR is the clearest example, a unit that only exists at the end, once the new path is in place.

sentences.en: The build order is only a rough draft of the split: the steps get regrouped and re-cut.
sentences.zh: 构建顺序只是拆分的粗略草稿：步骤被重新分组并重新剪切。

sentences.en: The deletion PR is the clearest example, a unit that only exists at the end, once the new path is in place.
sentences.zh: 删除 PR 是最明显的例子，一旦新路径就位，该单元仅存在于末尾。

blocks.html_en: I run one prompt:

sentences.en: I run one prompt:
sentences.zh: 我运行一个提示：

blocks.html_en: Split the current work into the smallest set of independently reviewable PRs, each safe to merge on its own, and each delivering value to the user whenever the work allows. Create a git worktree and branch off main for each. Stack only where a dependency is real; otherwise branch from main. Any removal of the code being replaced goes in its own final PR. Show me the proposed split before creating anything.

sentences.en: Split the current work into the smallest set of independently reviewable PRs, each safe to merge on its own, and each delivering value to the user whenever the work allows.
sentences.zh: 将当前工作拆分为最小的可独立审查的 PR 集，每个 PR 都可以安全地自行合并，并且只要工作允许，每个 PR 都会为用户提供价值。

sentences.en: Create a git worktree and branch off main for each.
sentences.zh: 创建一个 git 工作树并为每个工作树分支出主要分支。

sentences.en: Stack only where a dependency is real; otherwise branch from main.
sentences.zh: 仅在存在依赖关系的情况下才堆栈；否则从主分支分支。

sentences.en: Any removal of the code being replaced goes in its own final PR.
sentences.zh: 任何被替换代码的删除都会在其自己的最终 PR 中进行。

sentences.en: Show me the proposed split before creating anything.
sentences.zh: 在创建任何内容之前向我展示建议的拆分。

blocks.html_en: Split the current work into the smallest set of independently reviewable PRs, each safe to merge on its own, and each delivering value to the user whenever the work allows. Create a git worktree and branch off main for each. Stack only where a dependency is real; otherwise branch from main. Any removal of the code being replaced goes in its own final PR. Show me the proposed split before creating anything.

sentences.en: Split the current work into the smallest set of independently reviewable PRs, each safe to merge on its own, and each delivering value to the user whenever the work allows.
sentences.zh: 将当前工作拆分为最小的可独立审查的 PR 集，每个 PR 都可以安全地自行合并，并且只要工作允许，每个 PR 都会为用户提供价值。

sentences.en: Create a git worktree and branch off main for each.
sentences.zh: 创建一个 git 工作树并为每个工作树分支出主要分支。

sentences.en: Stack only where a dependency is real; otherwise branch from main.
sentences.zh: 仅在存在依赖关系的情况下才堆栈；否则从主分支分支。

sentences.en: Any removal of the code being replaced goes in its own final PR.
sentences.zh: 任何被替换代码的删除都会在其自己的最终 PR 中进行。

sentences.en: Show me the proposed split before creating anything.
sentences.zh: 在创建任何内容之前向我展示建议的拆分。

blocks.html_en: How long it takes depends on how tangled the work is, from a few minutes to a few rounds of back-and-forth. Either way, no manual cherry-picking.

sentences.en: How long it takes depends on how tangled the work is, from a few minutes to a few rounds of back-and-forth.
sentences.zh: 需要多长时间取决于工作的复杂程度，从几分钟到来回几轮。

sentences.en: Either way, no manual cherry-picking.
sentences.zh: 无论哪种方式，都不需要手动挑选。

blocks.html_en: That refactor came out as five PRs: two backend endpoints as siblings off main, two frontend views each sitting on top of the backend PR whose data it needs, and a final PR that was pure deletion of the old path. The deletion removed several hundred more lines than the whole feature added. That's the shape of a refactor done in this order.

sentences.en: That refactor came out as five PRs: two backend endpoints as siblings off main, two frontend views each sitting on top of the backend PR whose data it needs, and a final PR that was pure deletion of the old path.
sentences.zh: 该重构最终以五个 PR 的形式出现：两个后端端点作为主节点之外的兄弟节点，两个前端视图，每个前端视图都位于需要其数据的后端 PR 之上，最后一个 PR 纯粹删除了旧路径。

sentences.en: The deletion removed several hundred more lines than the whole feature added.
sentences.zh: 此次删除删除的行数比添加的整个功能多了数百行。

sentences.en: That's the shape of a refactor done in this order.
sentences.zh: 这就是按此顺序完成的重构的形式。

blocks.html_en: Two rules I've arrived at by doing this repeatedly:

sentences.en: Two rules I've arrived at by doing this repeatedly:
sentences.zh: 我通过反复这样做得出了两条规则：

blocks.html_en: Stack only when the dependency is real. A frontend view PR depends on its backend endpoint PR, and the branch reflects that. Everything else comes from main. Stacking for convenience creates a rebase chain you'll regret the moment the bottom PR gets feedback.

sentences.en: Stack only when the dependency is real.
sentences.zh: 仅当依赖关系真实时才堆栈。

sentences.en: A frontend view PR depends on its backend endpoint PR, and the branch reflects that.
sentences.zh: 前端视图 PR 取决于其后端端点 PR，分支反映了这一点。

sentences.en: Everything else comes from main.
sentences.zh: 其他一切都来自 main。

sentences.en: Stacking for convenience creates a rebase chain you'll regret the moment the bottom PR gets feedback.
sentences.zh: 为了方便而堆叠会创建一个 rebase 链，当底部 PR 得到反馈时，你会后悔的。

blocks.html_en: Cleanup ships last. The old code dies in its own PR, after the new path is live. Mixing deletion with creation confuses reviewers, makes rollback ambiguous, and buries the cleanup in the noise of the feature.

sentences.en: Cleanup ships last.
sentences.zh: 清理船最后。

sentences.en: The old code dies in its own PR, after the new path is live.
sentences.zh: 在新路径生效后，旧代码会在自己的 PR 中消失。

sentences.en: Mixing deletion with creation confuses reviewers, makes rollback ambiguous, and buries the cleanup in the noise of the feature.
sentences.zh: 将删除与创建混合在一起会使审阅者感到困惑，使回滚变得模糊，并将清理工作埋藏在功能的噪音中。

blocks.html_en: The split is also when I read my own work. Going through the diff PR by PR, at a size I can hold in my head, is the difference between having shipped AI-written code and understanding it. I'd rather find my own problems there.

sentences.en: The split is also when I read my own work.
sentences.zh: 分裂也是在我读自己的作品时。

sentences.en: Going through the diff PR by PR, at a size I can hold in my head, is the difference between having shipped AI-written code and understanding it.
sentences.zh: 以我能记住的大小逐一查看 PR 的差异，就是发布 AI 编写的代码和理解它之间的区别。

sentences.en: I'd rather find my own problems there.
sentences.zh: 我宁愿在那里找到我自己的问题。

blocks.html_en: One practical note: managing a stack burns context fast, so hand the split work to subagents that report back to a main agent. In Cursor, the split-to-prs skill packages this.

sentences.en: One practical note: managing a stack burns context fast, so hand the split work to subagents that report back to a main agent.
sentences.zh: 一个实用的注意事项：管理堆栈会快速消耗上下文，因此将拆分工作交给子代理，然后子代理向主代理报告。

sentences.en: In Cursor, the split-to-prs skill packages this.
sentences.zh: 在 Cursor 中， split-to prs 技能将其打包。

blocks.html_en: What it bought, what it costs

sentences.en: What it bought, what it costs
sentences.zh: 买了什么，花了多少钱

blocks.html_en: The heavy PRs stay heavy, and they should. The backend ones carried the real architectural risk (new data models, new API surface, trust boundaries), which is where reviewers should spend their attention. The frontend PRs that consume them read in minutes. Small, focused PRs flow. Large ones sit.

sentences.en: The heavy PRs stay heavy, and they should.
sentences.zh: 沉重的公关仍然很沉重，而且它们应该如此。

sentences.en: The backend ones carried the real architectural risk (new data models, new API surface, trust boundaries), which is where reviewers should spend their attention.
sentences.zh: 后端带来了真正的架构风险（新的数据模型、新的 API 界面、信任边界），这是审阅者应该关注的地方。

sentences.en: The frontend PRs that consume them read in minutes.
sentences.zh: 消耗它们的前端 PR 只需几分钟即可读取。

sentences.en: Small, focused PRs flow.
sentences.zh: 小而集中的公关流。

sentences.en: Large ones sit.
sentences.zh: 大的坐着。

blocks.html_en: The agent review loop is faster at this scale too. At Adapt, we use Adapt itself as a reviewer, an agent with business context from previous work. It comments within minutes of a PR opening, and the exchange (questions, clarifications, a small fix) resolves in under ten. That only works when a PR is small enough to read quickly; a 2,000-line PR mixing several concerns doesn't get that treatment from a human at all.

sentences.en: The agent review loop is faster at this scale too.
sentences.zh: 在这种规模下，代理审核循环也更快。

sentences.en: At Adapt, we use Adapt itself as a reviewer, an agent with business context from previous work.
sentences.zh: 在 Adapt，我们将 Adapt 本身用作审阅者，即具有先前工作中的业务背景的代理。

sentences.en: It comments within minutes of a PR opening, and the exchange (questions, clarifications, a small fix) resolves in under ten.
sentences.zh: 它会在公关开放后几分钟内发表评论，并且交流（问题、澄清、小修复）会在十分钟内解决。

sentences.en: That only works when a PR is small enough to read quickly; a 2,000-line PR mixing several concerns doesn't get that treatment from a human at all.
sentences.zh: 仅当 PR 小到足以快速阅读时，这才有效；一个 2,000 行的 PR 混合了几个问题，根本无法从人类那里得到这种待遇。

blocks.html_en: Merging incrementally also makes deployments easier to manage. If something breaks, you revert one focused change, and your error tracking points at that change instead of an entire merged stack.

sentences.en: Merging incrementally also makes deployments easier to manage.
sentences.zh: 增量合并还使部署更易于管理。

sentences.en: If something breaks, you revert one focused change, and your error tracking points at that change instead of an entire merged stack.
sentences.zh: 如果出现问题，您将恢复一个重点更改，并且您的错误跟踪将指向该更改而不是整个合并堆栈。

blocks.html_en: Those are the gains. Two costs come with them.

sentences.en: Those are the gains.
sentences.zh: 这些就是收获。

sentences.en: Two costs come with them.
sentences.zh: 随之而来的是两个成本。

blocks.html_en: Rebasing. When a reviewer asks for a change on a PR that another sits on, every branch above it needs rebasing. It doesn't happen often, since reviewers usually touch leaf PRs, but when it does you feel it. Keep the chat session that produced the split open: it still holds the split, so you can re-prompt it to update the branches above instead of doing it by hand.

sentences.en: Rebasing.
sentences.zh: 变基。

sentences.en: When a reviewer asks for a change on a PR that another sits on, every branch above it needs rebasing.
sentences.zh: 当审阅者要求对另一个审阅者所在的 PR 进行更改时，其上方的每个分支都需要重新定位。

sentences.en: It doesn't happen often, since reviewers usually touch leaf PRs, but when it does you feel it.
sentences.zh: 这种情况并不经常发生，因为审稿人通常会接触叶子 PR，但当它发生时你就会感觉到。

sentences.en: Keep the chat session that produced the split open: it still holds the split, so you can re-prompt it to update the branches above instead of doing it by hand.
sentences.zh: 保持生成拆分的聊天会话打开：它仍然保留拆分，因此您可以重新提示它更新上面的分支，而不是手动执行。

blocks.html_en: Splitting is not shipping. As I write this, all five PRs from that refactor are still open. A good split makes each PR easy to review and worth merging on its own. An agent does the first for me; the second is my call when I decide what goes in each PR, and my team's when they decide what to merge. Mine sat because I only did the first. Even if all five merge on the same day I keep the review benefit and a clean revert target per change; what I lose is incremental delivery, since nothing reached a user earlier and the deploys land as one batch.

sentences.en: Splitting is not shipping.
sentences.zh: 拆分不等于发货。

sentences.en: As I write this, all five PRs from that refactor are still open.
sentences.zh: 当我写这篇文章时，该重构的所有 5 个 PR 仍然处于开放状态。

sentences.en: A good split makes each PR easy to review and worth merging on its own.
sentences.zh: 良好的拆分使每个 PR 易于审查并且值得单独合并。

sentences.en: An agent does the first for me; the second is my call when I decide what goes in each PR, and my team's when they decide what to merge.
sentences.zh: 代理人为我做了第一件事；第二个是我在决定每个 PR 中包含哪些内容时的决定，以及我的团队在决定合并哪些内容时的决定。

sentences.en: Mine sat because I only did the first.
sentences.zh: 我的坐了因为我只做了第一个。

sentences.en: Even if all five merge on the same day I keep the review benefit and a clean revert target per change; what I lose is incremental delivery, since nothing reached a user earlier and the deploys land as one batch.
sentences.zh: 即使所有五个在同一天合并，我也会保留审查好处和每次更改的干净恢复目标；我失去的是增量交付，因为没有任何东西提前到达用户并且部署作为一批进行。

blocks.html_en: When to reach for it

sentences.en: When to reach for it
sentences.zh: 何时伸手去拿它

blocks.html_en: Good fit: multi-surface features crossing backend and frontend, refactors where you don't know the final shape until you've done it, any work where you'd otherwise be guessing at issue boundaries.

sentences.en: Good fit: multi-surface features crossing backend and frontend, refactors where you don't know the final shape until you've done it, any work where you'd otherwise be guessing at issue boundaries.
sentences.zh: 良好的配合：跨越后端和前端的多表面特征，在完成之前不知道最终形状的重构，以及任何您需要猜测问题边界的工作。

blocks.html_en: Harder fit: migrations and schema changes that must be sequenced in production, where the ordering is real and you should plan it first. Work that has one obvious place to cut. Features where step 1 cannot ship alone, ever; if everything lands at once, late decomposition buys you incremental review and nothing more.

sentences.en: Harder fit: migrations and schema changes that must be sequenced in production, where the ordering is real and you should plan it first.
sentences.zh: 更难适应：必须在生产中按顺序进行迁移和模式更改，其中顺序是真实的，您应该首先对其进行计划。

sentences.en: Work that has one obvious place to cut.
sentences.zh: 有一个明显需要删减的地方的工作。

sentences.en: Features where step 1 cannot ship alone, ever; if everything lands at once, late decomposition buys you incremental review and nothing more.
sentences.zh: 第 1 步永远无法单独发布的功能；如果一切都同时发生，那么后期的分解只会给你带来增量回顾，仅此而已。

blocks.html_en: The heuristic: if you're writing an RFC and guessing at how to break it into issues before you've built anything, that time is probably better spent building. You'll have better answers at the end. I've been testing this across a few projects and it has held up.

sentences.en: The heuristic: if you're writing an RFC and guessing at how to break it into issues before you've built anything, that time is probably better spent building.
sentences.zh: 启发式：如果您正在编写 RFC 并在构建任何内容之前猜测如何将其分解为问题，那么最好将时间花在构建上。

sentences.en: You'll have better answers at the end.
sentences.zh: 最后你会得到更好的答案。

sentences.en: I've been testing this across a few projects and it has held up.
sentences.zh: 我已经在几个项目中对此进行了测试，并且它已经成功。

blocks.html_en: The structural decision doesn't go away. It just gets much cheaper when you make it with the code already in front of you.

sentences.en: The structural decision doesn't go away.
sentences.zh: 结构性决策不会消失。

sentences.en: It just gets much cheaper when you make it with the code already in front of you.
sentences.zh: 当您使用面前的代码进行制作时，它会变得便宜得多。

content_html_zh:
优秀的工程师在建造之前做好计划。 我从小到大看到的工作流程：编写一个描述功能的 RFC，将其分成更小的问题，然后构建它们，每个问题通常都会阻碍下一个问题。 在一行代码出现之前，作品的结构就被锁定了。

这是合理的。 它使代码审查易于管理并避免大爆炸合并。 它还要求您在对问题了解最少的时刻做出最关键的结构性决策。

在构建任何东西之前，您会猜测：哪些部分是可分离的，每个部分有多复杂，步骤 3 是否会迫使您重新考虑步骤 1。 有时你是对的。 通常情况下，你不是这样的，所以第 1 步就被扔掉了。 你在构建它的过程中学到了一些东西，但是如果你先构建整个东西，你会学得更快。

我们支付这笔费用是有充分理由的：另一种选择是构建所有内容并手动解决它，而解决一周的工作比提前计划更困难。 预先确定边界从来不是为了让构建变得更容易。 这是为了让审查成为可能，而且这是实现这一目标的唯一经济实惠的方式。 这就是改变的部分。

发生了什么变化

三件事变得便宜得多。 构建：人工智能助手可以在几小时甚至几分钟内将一个明确的问题转化为工作代码。 设计：您可以询问计划并以对话速度重新制定计划。 这里最重要的是分解一个已完成的分支：将一周的混乱工作分解为一系列小的 PR 曾经是工作中最乏味的部分，这正是我们避免它的原因。 现在是提示。

有两件事并没有变得更便宜。 首先是Code Review的判断部分。 特工们使机械部分（一致性、缺陷、明显的错误）几乎免费，但他们没有解决微妙的正确性或围绕它的问题：这种变化是否属于它所在的位置，这个端点形状是否会在六个月后受到损害。 机器人批准你的 PR 与你理解代码不同，如果你没有输入代码，阅读它就是你拥有它的方式。 狭隘的 PR 使这种阅读成为可能。

二是产品验证。 运行这个东西并决定它是正确的构建仍然很慢。 新鲜的是让整个功能尽早发挥作用，在任何人阅读其中一行之前向其他人展示。

因此，停止预先确定边界以避免不再存在的成本。

我的工作流程现在如下所示：

  1. 仔细研究计划，直到其中有真正的决定
  2. 当设计新颖时，在任何代码之前提交规范
  3. 广泛构建，边走边提交保存点
  4. 在任何人阅读代码之前进行演示和迭代
  5. 沿着代码显示的边界分成 PR
  6. 最后合并、清理：在其自己的最终 PR 中进行纯删除

设计仍然是第一位

需要明确的是：这并不是“跳过计划并开始编码”。 在接触编辑器之前，我有一个计划，每个功能都从审问开始。 我会进行“烧烤”，这是一种在对抗性回合中就你的想法进行采访的技能，直到它做出真正的决定。 如果 API 调用失败，后备措施是什么？ 我对所有事情都运行它，包括小的变化，它不断地出现我不知道的差距。

当设计新颖时，计划就成为在任何代码之前提交的规范。 在另一个项目中，第一个 PR 是一个文档：功能是什么、它将如何工作、信任边界在哪里。 它在任何实施出现之前几天就合并了，因此团队可以先推迟。

永远不会被提交的是分解为 PR。 在构建之前决定构建什么；之后决定如何切片。

构建广泛

一旦设计确定，我就开始建造。 我经常按步骤工作，但我不会在每一步都停下来打开 PR 并等待审核。 所有内容都保留在一个分支上，直到它端到端地工作，无论任何文件都在其中。

承诺发生了，但对于其他人来说它们并不是里程碑。 它们是保存点：一个概念已被证明，或者我正要尝试一些冒险的事情并想要一根绳子拉回来。 我最近完成的一次重构在一天之内对数十个文件进行了十几次提交，并带有操作消息。 航点让我可以看到我去过的地方，而不是评论者的故事。

这是让一些工程师感到不舒服的部分，我明白为什么：git 历史应该是记录。 但这段历史永远不会成为记录。 最后的 PR 是从主干上新鲜切下来的，构建分支是你扔掉的草稿纸。 两个受众在时间上分开，我和审阅者，将他们分开可以让您针对两者进行优化。

在任何人阅读代码之前进行演示

一旦作品到位，我就会停下来展示它。 不是 PR 或代码审查，而是 Slack 中的短视频，或者预览部署（如果需要单击更改）。 在单个代码审查开始之前，使用该软件的人员对可用软件的反馈。

现在审查很昂贵，因为便宜的一半是自动化的。 在审核时发现您构建了错误的东西（令人困惑的 UI 模式、不适合前端使用数据方式的端点形状）会浪费审核者和您自己的时间。 演示可以捕捉到它，而更改的成本却很低。 如果出现需要重新思考的问题，我会首先对反馈进行“烧烤”，因此迭代不仅仅是共鸣。

船窄

构建顺序只是拆分的粗略草稿：步骤被重新分组并重新剪切。 删除 PR 是最明显的例子，一旦新路径就位，该单元仅存在于末尾。

我运行一个提示：

将当前工作拆分为最小的可独立审查的 PR 集，每个 PR 都可以安全地自行合并，并且只要工作允许，每个 PR 都会为用户提供价值。 创建一个 git 工作树并为每个工作树分支出主要分支。 仅在存在依赖关系的情况下才堆栈；否则从主分支分支。 任何被替换代码的删除都会在其自己的最终 PR 中进行。 在创建任何内容之前向我展示建议的拆分。

需要多长时间取决于工作的复杂程度，从几分钟到来回几轮。 无论哪种方式，都不需要手动挑选。

该重构最终以五个 PR 的形式出现：两个后端端点作为主节点之外的兄弟节点，两个前端视图，每个前端视图都位于需要其数据的后端 PR 之上，最后一个 PR 纯粹删除了旧路径。 此次删除删除的行数比添加的整个功能多了数百行。 这就是按此顺序完成的重构的形式。

我通过反复这样做得出了两条规则：

仅当依赖关系真实时才堆栈。 前端视图 PR 取决于其后端端点 PR，分支反映了这一点。 其他一切都来自 main。 为了方便而堆叠会创建一个 rebase 链，当底部 PR 得到反馈时，你会后悔的。

清理船最后。 在新路径生效后，旧代码会在自己的 PR 中消失。 将删除与创建混合在一起会使审阅者感到困惑，使回滚变得模糊，并将清理工作埋藏在功能的噪音中。

分裂也是在我读自己的作品时。 以我能记住的大小逐一查看 PR 的差异，就是发布 AI 编写的代码和理解它之间的区别。 我宁愿在那里找到我自己的问题。

一个实用的注意事项：管理堆栈会快速消耗上下文，因此将拆分工作交给子代理，然后子代理向主代理报告。 在 Cursor 中， split-to prs 技能将其打包。

买了什么，花了多少钱

沉重的公关仍然很沉重，而且它们应该如此。 后端带来了真正的架构风险（新的数据模型、新的 API 界面、信任边界），这是审阅者应该关注的地方。 消耗它们的前端 PR 只需几分钟即可读取。 小而集中的公关流。 大的坐着。

在这种规模下，代理审核循环也更快。 在 Adapt，我们将 Adapt 本身用作审阅者，即具有先前工作中的业务背景的代理。 它会在公关开放后几分钟内发表评论，并且交流（问题、澄清、小修复）会在十分钟内解决。 仅当 PR 小到足以快速阅读时，这才有效；一个 2,000 行的 PR 混合了几个问题，根本无法从人类那里得到这种待遇。

增量合并还使部署更易于管理。 如果出现问题，您将恢复一个重点更改，并且您的错误跟踪将指向该更改而不是整个合并堆栈。

这些就是收获。 随之而来的是两个成本。

变基。 当审阅者要求对另一个审阅者所在的 PR 进行更改时，其上方的每个分支都需要重新定位。 这种情况并不经常发生，因为审稿人通常会接触叶子 PR，但当它发生时你就会感觉到。 保持生成拆分的聊天会话打开：它仍然保留拆分，因此您可以重新提示它更新上面的分支，而不是手动执行。

拆分不等于发货。 当我写这篇文章时，该重构的所有 5 个 PR 仍然处于开放状态。 良好的拆分使每个 PR 易于审查并且值得单独合并。 代理人为我做了第一件事；第二个是我在决定每个 PR 中包含哪些内容时的决定，以及我的团队在决定合并哪些内容时的决定。 我的坐了因为我只做了第一个。 即使所有五个在同一天合并，我也会保留审查好处和每次更改的干净恢复目标；我失去的是增量交付，因为没有任何东西提前到达用户并且部署作为一批进行。

何时伸手去拿它

良好的配合：跨越后端和前端的多表面特征，在完成之前不知道最终形状的重构，以及任何您需要猜测问题边界的工作。

更难适应：必须在生产中按顺序进行迁移和模式更改，其中顺序是真实的，您应该首先对其进行计划。 有一个明显需要删减的地方的工作。 第 1 步永远无法单独发布的功能；如果一切都同时发生，那么后期的分解只会给你带来增量回顾，仅此而已。

启发式：如果您正在编写 RFC 并在构建任何内容之前猜测如何将其分解为问题，那么最好将时间花在构建上。 最后你会得到更好的答案。 我已经在几个项目中对此进行了测试，并且它已经成功。

结构性决策不会消失。 当您使用面前的代码进行制作时，它会变得便宜得多。
